kv-quantizado.d: Storing K and V (or the MLA latent) with fewer bits than BF16, typically FP8 with scales. It increases capacity in tokens (up to ~2× in FP8; less in practice, 1.70× in Qwen, because state, indexer and pages don't shrink) and reduces the bytes read per decode step, at the cost of an error that is written once and re-read in every following step.

fp8-e4m3.d: 8-bit floating point with 1 sign bit, 4 exponent bits and 3 mantissa bits (FN variant, no infinity). Maximum 448, smallest normal \(2^{-6}\), smallest subnormal \(2^{-9}\). Every E4M3 value is exactly representable in BF16 and FP16.

dequantizacao.d: The way back from quantization: multiplying the stored code by its group's scale (\(\hat x = s \cdot c\)) to get the number the kernel uses. It can be done in a separate tile or fused into the math (scale applied after the product).

escala-por-tensor.d: A single scale for an entire tensor, for example all of a layer's K (k_scale) and all of its V (v_scale). It costs zero bytes per token and comes out of the sums in the kernel, but one outlier stretches the scale of every number.

escala-calibrada.d: A scale measured offline by running samples through the model (the amax of K and V in each layer) and written into the checkpoint. Without it, vLLM uses 1.0 for per-tensor FP8 KV.

ue8m0.d: A 1-byte scale with no sign and no mantissa: it stores only an exponent with bias 127, and its value is \(2^{\text{byte}-127}\). Multiplying by it means adding to the exponent. DeepSeek-V4's KV uses one per 64-dim block, with the exponent rounded up.

upcast.d: Converting a number to a wider format (for example E4M3 → BF16 or FP16). When the target format contains every value of the source format, the conversion is exact and only the bit width changes.

reinterpretacao-de-bytes.d: Reading the same memory as another type, without copying or converting: tensor.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn) over a uint8 allocation. Reading FP8 bytes as BF16 would produce plausible garbage, which is why the QSA patch refuses that combination.

deriva-de-selecao.d: In sparse attention, quantization error in the keys changes the indexer's scores and swaps which blocks make the top-k. It gets worse with context, because there are more candidates near the cutoff, and it shows up as wrong answers, not as a crash.

cache-k-indexador.d: The keys that the lightweight indexer of a sparse attention stores to score candidates. In DeepSeek-V4 they are 132 B per compressed entry (1 every 4 tokens) across 21 layers, replicated on every rank; at 1M of context, they are the largest volume read per query token.

mxfp4.d: The OCP Microscaling format: FP4 E2M1 values in blocks of 32, each block with an E8M0 scale (a power of 2) computed with the floor of the exponent. That's ~4.25 bits per number.

nvfp4-ds-mla.d: The KV dtype used by the DeepSeek-V4 recipe. In the pinned image it is byte-for-byte identical to the 584 B fp8_ds_mla (448 FP8 + 128 B of BF16 RoPE + 8 B of scales). Only the kernel dispatch and the spec's alignment change; it is not a 4-bit KV.

despacho-de-kernel.d: The runtime choice of which kernel runs the operation, often by comparing the dtype's name. Two names with the same bytes can land on different kernels, as in DeepSeek's bug #22 (1.0 versus 17.3 tok/s at 600K+).

qat.d: Training while simulating quantization (quantizing and dequantizing in the forward pass) so that the model learns to tolerate the rounding. DeepSeek-V4 trained its NoPE KV this way in FP8 with blocks of 64, and its indexer in FP4, so serving in those formats is the training regime.

linha-de-kv.d: The record written per token (and per layer) in an MLA/MQA-style KV, with values, scales, BF16 parts and padding. Examples: 656 B in the fp8_ds_mla of V3.2/GLM, 584 B in DeepSeek-V4 and 528 B in the kv8 of the GLM TensorFold lane.

pagina-uniforme.d: A rule of vLLM's hybrid allocator: every KV group uses pages with the same number of bytes, because pages come out of a single pool and serve any group. In DeepSeek-V4 the page is 64 × 584 = 37,376 B; according to the recipe's design document, a new row is only cheap if it divides the page into a whole, power-of-2 number of rows.

dcp.d: Parallelism that splits the KV tokens across ranks, instead of replicating them, and combines the partial attentions. It is exact and would double the MLA KV capacity in TP2, but it isn't enabled for the DeepSeek-V4 backends in the recipe's image.

kv8.d: The row format of the FP8 KV in the GLM TensorFold lane (patch 0038): 512 E4M3 codes, one power-of-two FP32 scale (\(2^{\lceil \log_2 \text{amax} \rceil - 8}\), so nothing saturates) and 12 zero bytes that align the row to 16 B, for a total of 528 B. Since the scale covers the whole row and is a power of two, the kernel applies it after the product without rounding anything.
